327019.title: The Schenker prime valuation-tree conjecture
327019.statement:
Let $a_n=\sum_{j=0}^{n}\frac{n!}{j!}n^j$ for $n\in\mathbb{N}_+$, and call an odd prime $p$ a **Schenker prime** when $p\mid a_n$ for some positive integer $n$ with $p\nmid n$. Let $v_p$ denote the $p$-adic valuation. **The Schenker prime valuation-tree conjecture.** For every odd Schenker prime $p$ and every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists a unique solution modulo $p^k$ of the inequality

$$
v_p(a_n)\geq k
$$

that is not congruent to $0$ modulo $p$. This conjecture predicts a unique nonzero residue branch modulo every power of an odd Schenker prime; the surrounding text presents it as a more general conjecture attributed to the authors of the cited work, while the paper's theorem supplies lifting criteria in terms of $q_{n_k,p}$ but does not state that this conjecture is proved.

327069.title: Gasarch–Hirst graph-colouring conjecture
327069.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\ell,k\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\mathrm{COL}(\ell,k,G)$ denote the statement that if $G$ is locally $\ell$-colorable, then $G$ is globally $k$-colorable. Here $\mathrm{RCA}_0$ is the base theory of recursive comprehension and $\mathrm{WKL}$ is weak König's lemma.

**Gasarch–Hirst conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{RCA}_0\vdash (\forall \ell\geq 2)(\forall k\geq \ell)(\mathrm{WKL}\leftrightarrow\forall G\,\mathrm{COL}(\ell,k,G)).
$$

The conjecture generalizes Gasarch and Hirst's theorem, which establishes the corresponding equivalence with $k=2\ell-1$. It asks whether every finite increase from the number of colors guaranteed locally to any $k\geq\ell$ yields the same reverse-mathematical strength as weak König's lemma.

327142.title: Bounded diameter conjecture for connected proper power graphs
327142.statement:
For a finite group $G$, let $bdom? \mathcal{P}^*(G)$ denote its proper power graph, and suppose that this graph is connected. **Bounded diameter conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that, for every finite group $G$ with connected proper power graph,

$$
\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{P}^*(G))\leq c.
$$

The preceding results on proper power graphs of finite groups motivate this uniform boundedness question; the conjecture asserts that connected proper power graphs have diameters bounded independently of the group.

327206.title: The p-spectral Turán conjecture for k-chromatic uniform hypergraphs
327206.statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-chromatic $r$-graph of order $n$, where $k\geq 2$ and $n>(r-1)k$. For $p\geq 1$, write $\lambda^{(p)}(G)$ for the $p$-spectral radius of $G$, and let $Q_k^r(n)$ denote the complete $k$-chromatic $r$-graph of order $n$. **The p-spectral Turán conjecture.** For every $p\geq 1$, 

$$
\lambda^{(p)}(G)<\lambda^{(p)}\left(Q_k^r(n)\right),
$$

unless $G=Q_k^r(n)$. This conjecture proposes the extremal $p$-spectral radius among $k$-chromatic $r$-graphs in the range $n>(r-1)k$, extending the preceding theorem from $3$-graphs; the generalization was posed because the authors' methods do not handle this range.

327299.title: Existence of arbitrarily long S-crucial permutations with respect to squares
327299.statement: Let an **S-crucial permutation with respect to squares** be a permutation that is crucial for the property of avoiding squares, with $S$ denoting the relevant permutation property. **S-crucial existence conjecture.** There exist arbitrary long S-crucial permutations with respect to squares. This is one of the open questions posed alongside the search for missing exact solutions in the reported tables.

327364.title: The order conjecture for birational rowmotion on northeast triangular posets
327364.statement:
Let $\operatorname*{NEtri}(p)$ be the northeast triangular poset of the triangular poset construction, and let $R_{\operatorname*{NEtri}(p)}$ denote birational rowmotion on it. For a birational map $R$, write $\operatorname*{ord}(R)$ for its order. **The northeast triangular order conjecture.** For every integer $p>1$, 

$$
\operatorname*{ord}\left(R_{\operatorname*{NEtri}(p)}\right)=p.
$$

The conjectured orders were verified using Sage for small values of $p$; later in the supplied text, the odd-$p$ case is proved, but no resolution of the full all-$p$ statement is supplied here.

327443.title: Shephard's dimension-preserving subpolytope conjecture
327443.statement:
A **stacked polytope** is a polytope obtained by repeatedly stacking simplices. A **subpolytope** is the convex hull of a subset of the vertices of a polytope. A combinatorial type records the face-incidence structure.

**Shephard's conjecture.** For every $d\ge 0$, every combinatorial type of $d$-dimensional polytope can be realized using subpolytopes of $d$-dimensional stacked polytopes.

The conjecture is the combinatorial form of Shephard's question after his geometric version was shown to be false; the source gives no resolution.

330334.title: Finite classification conjecture for graphs of bounded algebraic co-rank
330334.statement:
For $k\geq1$, let

$$
\Gamma_{\leq k}=\{G: G\text{ is a simple connected graph with }\gamma(G)\leq k\},
$$

and let $\mathcal{T}_{\delta}^*(G)$ denote the set of induced subgraphs of one graph in $\mathcal{T}_{\delta}(G)$. **Finite classification conjecture.** For every $k\geq1$,

$$
\Gamma_{\leq k}=\bigcup_{(G,\delta)\in\mathcal{G}}\mathcal{T}_{\delta}^*(G)
$$

for some finite set $\mathcal{G}$ of pairs $(G,\delta)$, where $G$ is a simple graph and $\delta\in\{0,1,-1\}^{V(G)}$. This extends the known classifications for algebraic co-rank at most two and three; the general finite classification remains conjectural.

330335.title: Eventual family conjecture for nested graphs of bounded algebraic co-rank
330335.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}=\{G_i\}_{i=1}^{\infty}$ be an infinite family of simple graphs such that $G_i$ is a proper induced subgraph of $G_j$ for all $i<j$. **Eventual family conjecture.** Either

$$
\max\{\gamma_{\mathcal P}(G_i)\}_{i=1}^{\infty}=\infty,
$$

or there exist a graph $G$, a vector $\delta\in\{0,1,-1\}^{V(G)}$, and an integer $M\in\mathbb N$ such that $G_i\in\mathcal{T}_{\delta}(G)$ for all $i\geq M$. This is presented as a weak form of the finite classification conjecture and remains open.

330501.title: The collapse conjecture for the sutured-annular-to-Khovanov spectral sequence
330501.statement:
Let $W_k$ denote the invariants in the decomposition associated with the spectral sequence from sutured annular Khovanov homology to ordinary Khovanov homology. **Collapse conjecture.** The spectral sequence collapses immediately, and

$$
W_k=0\qquad\text{for all }k\geq2.
$$

The conjecture predicts that no higher invariants survive beyond the immediate page of the spectral sequence. The supplied text gives no resolution or further evidence about its status.

330528.title: Frankl–Rödl/Frankl–Wilson conjecture with sum restrictions
330528.statement: For $S\subset[n]$, write $\lVert S\rVert=\sum_{s\in S}s$. Let $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\beta_1,\beta_2$ satisfy $0<\alpha_1,\alpha_2<1$ and $0<\beta_1,\beta_2<1$, and let $\mathcal G$ be the family of subsets $S\subset[n]$ with $|S|=[\alpha_1n]$ and $\lVert S\rVert=[\alpha_2\binom n2]$. Let $X$ count pairs $A,B\in\mathcal G$ whose intersection $C$ satisfies $|C|=[\beta_1n]$ and $\lVert C\rVert=[\beta_2\binom n2]$. **Frankl–Rödl/Frankl–Wilson conjecture with sum restrictions.** For every $\epsilon>0$, there is $\delta>0$ such that every subfamily $F\subseteq\mathcal G$ with $|F|>(1-\delta)^n|\mathcal G|$ contains at least $(1-\epsilon)^nX$ such pairs. The source notes that Eoin Long reduced many cases to the original Frankl–Rödl theorem, but does not resolve the conjecture in full.

330821.title: Bang-Jensen–Gutin–Li hamiltonicity conjecture for dominating pairs
330821.statement:
Let $D$ be a finite strong digraph without loops or multiple arcs on $n$ vertices. For distinct vertices $x,y$, write $x\rightarrow y$ when there is an arc from $x$ to $y$. A pair of vertices is **dominating** if both vertices send an arc to a common vertex, and a pair is **dominated** if a common vertex sends an arc to both of them. Here $d(x)$ denotes the degree of $x$.

**Bang-Jensen–Gutin–Li conjecture.** If

$$
d(x)+d(y)\geq 2n-1
$$

for every pair of dominating non-adjacent vertices and every pair of dominated non-adjacent vertices $\{x,y\}$, then $D$ is hamiltonian.

This conjecture was raised by Bang-Jensen, Gutin and Li as a degree-sum condition combining local domination structure with hamiltonicity. It is still open and seems quite difficult.

330961.title: One-high-vertex conjecture for fixable trees
330961.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree and let $f:V(T)\to\mathbb N$ satisfy $f(v)\geq d_T(v)$ for every vertex $v$. A tree is **$f$-fixable** if it is fixable for every list assignment whose lists have size at least $f(v)$ and satisfy the relevant superabundance condition.

**One-high-vertex conjecture.** The tree $T$ is $f$-fixable if $f(v)=d_T(v)$ for at most one non-leaf vertex $v$ of $T$.

The conjecture would imply, under the same degree constraints, that Tashkinov trees are elementary. It is presented as open in the surrounding discussion, with paths mentioned as a simpler special case.

330962.title: Moonshine conjecture on strict degree surplus and fixability
330962.statement:
Let $G$ be a multigraph and let $f:V(G)\to\mathbb N$ be a degree bound. The graph is **$f$-fixable** if it is fixable for the relevant list assignments with list sizes at least $f(v)$.

**Moonshine conjecture.** If

$$
f(v)>d_G(v)\quad\text{for all }v\in V(G),
$$

then $G$ is $f$-fixable.

The paper explicitly states that this conjecture is false and discusses counterexamples, including that $C_5$ is not $f$-fixable for any function $f$.

330963.title: Star-with-one-edge-subdivided fixability conjecture
330963.statement:
Let $G$ be a star with one edge subdivided. Let $r$ be its center, $t$ the vertex at distance two from $r$, and $s$ the intervening vertex. Let $L$ be a superabundant list assignment with $|L(v)|\geq d_G(v)$ for every $v\in V(G)$, and let $\psi_L(G)$ denote the paper's potential parameter.

**Star-with-one-edge-subdivided conjecture.** The graph $G$ is $L$-fixable if at least one of the following holds:

1. $|L(r)|>d_G(r)$;
2. $|L(s)|>d_G(s)$; or
3. $\psi_L(G)>|E(G)|$.

This conjecture generalizes the short Kierstead Paths of Kostochka and Stiebitz. Parts (a) and (b) are special cases of the one-high-vertex conjecture; the authors report a draft proof for (a), while (b) and (c) remain open in the paper.

331147.title: Kupek, Petrovic, and Yero's torus EOD-graph conjecture
331147.statement:
Let $C_r$ and $C_t$ be cycles, and let $C_r\,\Box\,C_t$ denote their Cartesian product, also called a torus. A graph is an **efficient open domination graph** (EOD-graph) if it has a set $D$ such that

$$
\bigcup_{v\in D}N(v)=V(G)
$$

and $N(u)\cap N(v)=\emptyset$ for every pair of distinct vertices $u,v\in D$.

**Kupek, Petrovic, and Yero's torus EOD-graph conjecture.** Let $r$ and $t$ be integers such that $r\geq 3$ and $t\geq 3$. The torus $C_r\,\Box\,C_t$ is an EOD-graph if and only if

$$
r\equiv 0\pmod{4}\quad\text{and}\quad t\equiv 0\pmod{4}.
$$

The conjecture is based on known characterizations for parallel EOD-sets and certain grid, torus, and cylinder families; the source gives no evidence that the full torus characterization has been resolved.

331434.title: Uniform rank-symmetric chain partition conjecture for the Boolean lattice
331434.statement:
Let $h$ be a positive integer. Let $N(h)$ be a positive integer depending on $h$, and let $n$ be an odd positive integer.

**Uniform rank-symmetric chain conjecture.** For every positive integer $h$ there exists a positive integer $N(h)$ such that, whenever $n>N(h)$ and $n$ is odd, the Boolean lattice $2^{[n]}$ has a partition into rank-symmetric chains in which all but at most one chain have size $2h$.

This is the rank-symmetric analogue of a result of Lonc concerning partitions into chains of almost uniform size. The source presents it as an open problem, and gives no resolution.

331440.title: The DC-set {x+y,xy} conjecture
331440.statement:
Let $E\subset\mathbb{N}$ be a $DC$ set, meaning a set with the central-set property referred to in the source. **The $DC$-set $\{x+y,xy\}$ conjecture.** The set $E$ contains a configuration of the form

$$
\{x+y,xy\}.
$$

Every finite partition of a $DC$ set has a $DC$ cell, and $DC$ sets are both additively and multiplicatively piecewise syndetic. The conjecture would therefore provide a configuration result in a class stable under finite partitions, but it remains open.

331551.title: Fang–Li–Wang–Xu conjecture on cubic graphical regular representations
331551.statement: Let $G$ be a finite nonabelian simple group. A **cubic graphical regular representation** (GRR) of $G$ is a Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(G,S)$ of valency three whose automorphism group is the right regular representation of $G$. **Fang–Li–Wang–Xu's conjecture.** Every finite nonabelian simple group has a cubic GRR. This conjecture concerns the existence of prescribed-valency GRRs; the paper studies it for the family $\mathrm{PSL}_2(q)$ and establishes existence there except when $q=7$, so the assertion remains open in general.

350219.title: Frid–Puzynina–Zamboni prefix palindromic-length conjecture
350219.statement: Let $w$ be an infinite word. A **prefix of arbitrarily high palindromic length** means that for every integer $M$ there is a prefix $u$ of $w$ with $\operatorname{PL}(u)\geq M$. **Frid–Puzynina–Zamboni's prefix conjecture.** Every non-ultimately periodic infinite word has prefixes of arbitrarily high palindromic length. This is an equivalent formulation of the bounded palindromic length conjecture; the paper states that the latter remains open in general.
